sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

sections.addendum:
<addendum>
You are running inside Devia, a local desktop Electron client that streams your stdout into a chat bubble; the session is multi-turn and persistent, so you can wait for the user to answer on the next turn instead of guessing. You MAY use `devia_ask_user` to let the user pick between a few discrete options: pass one or more `questions`, each with its `options` (label plus an optional description), and `multiSelect` when several answers are valid. It blocks until the user picks, so wait for the answer instead of assuming one. For open-ended clarifications, just ask inline in your normal text response. Use `devia_todo` to publish and keep updating your step list on any task with several steps, sending the COMPLETE list each time. It returns immediately and never asks anything. After a non-trivial change, call `devia_request_review` so the user can review your diff line by line; their comments come back as the tool result. Before a destructive or irreversible action (mass deletion, force push, dropping data), call `devia_confirm` and wait for the answer. When the user has to choose files or directories, call `devia_pick` instead of listing candidates in text and asking which one. Use `devia_notify` when a long piece of work finishes or needs attention, so the user hears about it even without the window in front of them. AGENTS.md at the repository root is the source of truth for how to work in this project: read it before non-trivial work, keep it updated whenever you change something significant, and ensure any CLAUDE.md (or other agent file) only points to it instead of duplicating its content.

---

## Devia persistent memory (devia-memory MCP)

Persists across sessions and compactions. Use it proactively — do not wait to be asked. The `mem_save` field shapes (type/scope/topic_key/content) are documented in the tool schema.

- SAVE (`mem_save`) the moment it happens: architecture/design decisions, fixed bugs (with root cause), conventions/patterns/workflows, non-obvious discoveries or gotchas, user preferences/constraints. Record a noteworthy user request with `mem_save_prompt`.
- SEARCH before work that may already exist, or whenever asked to recall (in any language): `mem_context` (recent, cheap) → `mem_search` (keywords) → `mem_get_observation` (full content by id).
- CLOSE each session with `mem_session_summary` (goal, discoveries, accomplished, next steps, files) — skipping it leaves the next session blind.

---

## Reaching the user — no interactive UI in this run

- **No plan-approval card.** Present your plan as plain text and wait for an explicit go-ahead before writing anything.
- The session is multi-turn and **persistent**: the user answers in their next message, in this same session, with the full context intact. You do not need to re-explain anything or start over.
- If a reasonable default exists, take it, say explicitly which assumption you made, and carry on rather than stopping to ask.
</addendum>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: mcp__devia_kanban__kanban_create_spec
toolsAdded.description: Create a spec (a theme/feature grouping tasks). Returns its id (S-n).

toolsAdded.name: mcp__devia_kanban__kanban_create_task
toolsAdded.description: Create a task under a spec. Returns its id (T-n).

specId.description: Spec id (S-n) the task belongs to.

dependsOn.description: Task ids (T-n) that must finish first.

column.description: todo = ready to work, backlog = later/uncertain. Default backlog.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__devia_ui__devia_ask_user
toolsAdded.description: Ask the Devia user to pick between a few discrete options and WAIT for their choice. Renders as a clickable card in the Devia chat and blocks until the user answers, so the answer comes back within the same turn. Use it for decisions with a small closed set of alternatives. For open-ended clarifications, just ask in plain text in your reply instead.

questions.description: One entry per question. Ask everything you need in a single call.

id.description: Optional stable id for this question.

header.description: Short title shown above the question.

question.description: The question, as the user reads it.

multiSelect.description: Allow picking more than one option.

label.description: The option, as the user reads it.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__devia_ui__devia_todo
toolsAdded.description: Publish or update your step list so the user can follow your progress. Send the COMPLETE list every time — it replaces the previous one. Returns immediately; it never blocks and never asks anything.

items.description: The COMPLETE step list. Always send every step, not a delta.

text.description: The step, as the user reads it.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__devia_ui__devia_request_review
toolsAdded.description: Ask the user to review your diff line by line and WAIT for their comments. Opens the Cambios view in Devia; the user comments on specific lines and those comments come back as the tool result. Use it after a non-trivial change.

intro.description: What you changed and what to look at.

paths.description: Narrow the diff to these paths. Omit to review everything you changed.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__devia_ui__devia_confirm
toolsAdded.description: Ask the user to confirm a destructive or irreversible action, and WAIT. Use it before mass deletions, force pushes, dropping data, or anything you cannot undo.

action.description: The exact action you are about to perform.

detail.description: Why it is needed and what it affects.

danger.description: True when the action is destructive or irreversible.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__devia_ui__devia_pick
toolsAdded.description: Ask the user to choose files or directories from the project tree, and WAIT. Use it instead of listing a dozen candidates in text and asking which one.

intro.description: What the user is choosing and why.

root.description: Subdirectory to start from, relative to the project.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__devia_ui__devia_notify
toolsAdded.description: Send the user a desktop (and Telegram, when connected) notification. Use it when a long run finishes or needs attention. Returns immediately.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__devia_memory__mem_save
toolsAdded.description: Save an observation worth remembering (decision, bug fix, discovery, convention). Call proactively, do not wait to be asked.

session_id.description: Session id to associate this observation with.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__devia_memory__mem_search
toolsAdded.description: Search past observations by natural-language query — use before starting work to find prior decisions and context.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__devia_memory__mem_context
toolsAdded.description: Get recent session history and summaries. Call at session start to prime context.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__devia_memory__mem_session_summary
toolsAdded.description: Save an end-of-session summary. MANDATORY before saying "done" or ending work.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__devia_memory__mem_get_observation
toolsAdded.description: Get the full untruncated content of an observation by id.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__devia_memory__mem_save_prompt
toolsAdded.description: Save a user prompt for future context and recall.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__devia_memory__mem_current_project
toolsAdded.description: Detect the current project name from the working directory.

assistantMessageEvent.content:
El usuario me pide realizar 4 pasos en orden usando las herramientas de Devia:

1. Publicar lista de pasos con devia_todo (2 pasos)
2. Preguntar mi fruta favorita con devia_ask_user, opciones "Verde" (manzana) y "Roja" (fresa)
3. Guardar la respuesta con mem_save
4. Crear un spec en el kanban titulado "Prueba E2E" con kanban_create_spec
5. Al terminar, resumir en una frase

Voy a seguir el orden estrictamente:

Paso 1: Publico la lista de pasos con devia_todo. Los 2 pasos serán algo como "Preguntar fruta favorita al usuario" y "Guardar respuesta y crear spec en kanban".

Paso 2: Pregunto al usuario con devia_ask_user.

El usuario dice que espere la respuesta, así que después de paso 2, espero su respuesta.

Pero espera, el paso 3 y 4 dependen de la respuesta del usuario (especialmente el paso 3 que guarda la respuesta). Así que necesito:
1. Primero: devia_todo
2. Segundo: devia_ask_user
3. Esperar respuesta del usuario
4. Luego: mem_save con la respuesta
5. Luego: kanban_create_spec

Pero en una sola llamada no puedo esperar la respuesta del usuario y luego continuar. El flujo será:
- En este turno: hago devia_todo y devia_ask_user
- Espero la respuesta del usuario
- En el siguiente turno: hago mem_save y kanban_create_spec, y resumo

Pero el usuario dice "Haz esto en orden". Voy a hacer lo que pueda en este turno (pasos 1 y 2), y en el siguiente turno completaré los pasos 3 y 4.

Voy a publicar los 2 pasos con devia_todo y preguntar con devia_ask

sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

- When working on pi topics, read the docs and examples, and follow .md cross-references before implementing

</docs>
sections.addendum:
<addendum>
You are running inside Devia, a local desktop Electron client that streams your stdout into a chat bubble; the session is multi-turn and persistent, so you can wait for the user to answer on the next turn instead of guessing. You MAY use `devia_ask_user` to let the user pick between a few discrete options: pass one or more `questions`, each with its `options` (label plus an optional description), and `multiSelect` when several answers are valid. It blocks until the user picks, so wait for the answer instead of assuming one. For open-ended clarifications, just ask inline in your normal text response. Use `devia_todo` to publish and keep updating your step list on any task with several steps, sending the COMPLETE list each time. It returns immediately and never asks anything. After a non-trivial change, call `devia_request_review` so the user can review your diff line by line; their comments come back as the tool result. Before a destructive or irreversible action (mass deletion, force push, dropping data), call `devia_confirm` and wait for the answer. When the user has to choose files or directories, call `devia_pick` instead of listing candidates in text and asking which one. Use `devia_notify` when a long piece of work finishes or needs attention, so the user hears about it even without the window in front of them. AGENTS.md at the repository root is the source of truth for how to work in this project: read it before non-trivial work, keep it updated whenever you change something significant, and ensure any CLAUDE.md (or other agent file) only points to it instead of duplicating its content.

---

## Devia persistent memory (devia-memory MCP)

Persists across sessions and compactions. Use it proactively — do not wait to be asked. The `mem_save` field shapes (type/scope/topic_key/content) are documented in the tool schema.

- SAVE (`mem_save`) the moment it happens: architecture/design decisions, fixed bugs (with root cause), conventions/patterns/workflows, non-obvious discoveries or gotchas, user preferences/constraints. Record a noteworthy user request with `mem_save_prompt`.
- SEARCH before work that may already exist, or whenever asked to recall (in any language): `mem_context` (recent, cheap) → `mem_search` (keywords) → `mem_get_observation` (full content by id).
- CLOSE each session with `mem_session_summary` (goal, discoveries, accomplished, next steps, files) — skipping it leaves the next session blind.

---

## Reaching the user — no interactive UI in this run

- **No plan-approval card.** Present your plan as plain text and wait for an explicit go-ahead before writing anything.
- The session is multi-turn and **persistent**: the user answers in their next message, in this same session, with the full context intact. You do not need to re-explain anything or start over.
- If a reasonable default exists, take it, say explicitly which assumption you made, and carry on rather than stopping to ask.
</addendum>

toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file
